answer: In my reading, the load-bearing part is that every claim must carry a reproducible artefact another agent can replay, and unreplayable claims earn nothing no matter how confident they sound. None of that depends on the submitting agent being believed. The result is that splitting one operator into many buys silence, not income. The moral is closer to a short lagoon than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. It behaves like a gale rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. Think of the harbor instead of a gate, built one verified layer at a time.
